subject: BAR
title: Standard Cost Variances and Sales Price, Volume, and Mix Analysis
scenario:
Calderon Outdoor Products, Inc. manufactures two lines of powered hand tools: the Ridgeline line, produced at the Bellwether plant, and the Summit line, produced at the Kearny plant. The company uses a standard cost system and reviews its manufacturing and selling variances each month.

You are assisting the corporate controller with the March Year 6 operating review. Production cost variances for the month have been requested for the Ridgeline line only, because the Kearny plant reports its manufacturing results on a different closing calendar. Standard cost data appear in **Exhibit 1**, the March manufacturing results of the Bellwether plant appear in **Exhibit 2**, and budgeted and actual sales data for both product lines appear in **Exhibit 3**.

March unit sales of the Ridgeline line exceeded March production; the difference was filled from beginning finished goods inventory. Use only the data provided, do not round intermediate amounts, and state all answers in whole dollars.

exhibits.title: Exhibit 1: Standard Cost Cards
exhibits.content:
**Ridgeline line — Bellwether plant (standard cost per unit)**

| Cost element | Standard quantity | Standard price or rate | Standard cost per unit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Direct materials | 4.00 pounds | $6.50 per pound | $26.00 |
| Direct labor | 1.50 direct labor hours | $22.00 per hour | $33.00 |
| Variable manufacturing overhead | 1.50 direct labor hours | $9.00 per hour | $13.50 |
| Fixed manufacturing overhead | 1.50 direct labor hours | $12.00 per hour | $18.00 |
| **Total standard cost per unit** | | | **$90.50** |

Variable and fixed manufacturing overhead are applied to the Ridgeline line on the basis of direct labor hours. The fixed overhead rate was set from a monthly fixed overhead budget of $216,000 and denominator activity of 18,000 direct labor hours.

**Summit line — Kearny plant (standard cost per unit)**

| Cost element | Standard quantity | Standard price or rate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Direct materials | 6.00 pounds | $7.25 per pound |
| Direct labor | 2.00 direct labor hours | $24.50 per hour |
| Variable manufacturing overhead | 2.00 direct labor hours | $10.00 per hour |

exhibits.title: Exhibit 2: Bellwether Plant — March Year 6 Manufacturing Results (Ridgeline line)
exhibits.content:
| Item | Amount |
| --- | --- |
| Units completed | 12,000 units |
| Direct materials purchased and placed into production | 50,400 pounds |
| Actual direct materials cost | $6.70 per pound |
| Actual direct labor hours worked | 17,600 hours |
| Actual direct labor cost | $394,240 |
| Actual variable manufacturing overhead incurred | $163,680 |
| Actual fixed manufacturing overhead incurred | $221,400 |

No direct materials were held in the storeroom at the beginning or the end of March; every pound purchased during the month was placed into production.

Plant notes for March:

- The contracted steel supplier missed its March delivery. Purchasing covered the requirement on the spot market at a premium, and the spot lots were an off-specification grade. The plant reported scrap above the standard allowance.
- To protect the delivery schedule, the plant scheduled a larger share of senior operators, whose hourly rates are above the standard rate.

exhibits.title: Exhibit 3: Budgeted and Actual Sales — March Year 6
exhibits.content:
| Product line | Budgeted units | Budgeted selling price per unit | Budgeted contribution margin per unit | Actual units sold | Actual average selling price per unit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Ridgeline | 12,000 | $95.00 | $30.00 | 14,300 | $92.50 |
| Summit | 8,000 | $140.00 | $50.00 | 7,700 | $143.00 |
| **Total** | **20,000** | | | **22,000** | |

The Ridgeline average selling price reflects a promotional discount offered through a national retailer during March. Budgeted fixed selling and administrative expenses for March were $310,000.

tasks.title: Direct Materials Price Variance
tasks.instruction: Compute the direct materials price variance for the Ridgeline line for March Year 6 (in whole dollars, no commas). Enter an unfavorable variance as a positive number and a favorable variance as a negative number.
tasks.explanation:
The direct materials price variance is (actual price - standard price) x actual quantity purchased and used.

Actual price: $6.70 per pound. Standard price: $6.50 per pound. Difference: $0.20 per pound.
Actual quantity purchased and placed into production: 50,400 pounds.

Variance: $0.20 x 50,400 = $10,080. The price paid exceeded the standard price, so the variance is unfavorable and is entered as a positive $10,080.
tasks.explanationJa:
直接材料価格差異 =（実際単価 − 標準単価）× 実際購入・投入数量

1. 単価差: $6.70 − $6.50 = $0.20/ポンド
2. 実際数量: 50,400ポンド（月初・月末の材料在庫はなく、購入量＝投入量）
3. 差異: $0.20 × 50,400 = **$10,080**

実際単価が標準単価を上回っているため**不利差異（U）**。約束どおり正の数 10080 を入力する。

価格差異は「購入量（ここでは投入量と同じ）」に単価差を掛ける点に注意する。生産量から計算した標準許容量（48,000ポンド）を使うのは数量差異の側である。
references: Cost accounting — standard costing: direct materials price variance

tasks.title: Direct Materials Quantity Variance
tasks.instruction: Compute the direct materials quantity (usage) variance for the Ridgeline line for March Year 6 (in whole dollars, no commas). Enter an unfavorable variance as a positive number and a favorable variance as a negative number.
tasks.explanation:
The direct materials quantity variance is (actual quantity used - standard quantity allowed for actual output) x standard price.

Standard quantity allowed: 12,000 units completed x 4.00 pounds = 48,000 pounds.
Actual quantity used: 50,400 pounds.
Excess usage: 50,400 - 48,000 = 2,400 pounds.

Variance: 2,400 x $6.50 standard price = $15,600 unfavorable, entered as a positive $15,600. The quantity variance is measured at the standard price so that the price effect stays in the price variance.
tasks.explanationJa:
直接材料数量差異 =（実際消費量 − 実際生産量に対する標準許容量）× **標準**単価

1. 標準許容量: 12,000個 × 4.00ポンド = 48,000ポンド
2. 実際消費量: 50,400ポンド
3. 超過量: 50,400 − 48,000 = 2,400ポンド
4. 差異: 2,400 × $6.50 = **$15,600**

標準より多く消費しているため**不利差異（U）**。正の数 15600 を入力する。

数量差異は**標準単価**で評価する（実際単価 $6.70 を使わない）。実際単価との差は価格差異側で既に切り出しているため、ここで実際単価を使うと価格効果を二重計上することになる。

なお直接材料の総差異は $10,080 + $15,600 = $25,680 の不利差異であり、実際原価 50,400 × $6.70 = $337,680 と標準原価 48,000 × $6.50 = $312,000 の差と一致する。
references: Cost accounting — standard costing: direct materials quantity variance

tasks.title: Direct Labor and Variable Overhead Variance Schedule
tasks.instruction: Complete the schedule of direct labor and variable manufacturing overhead variances for the Ridgeline line for March Year 6. In the Amount column, enter each variance as a positive amount in whole dollars, with no commas and no minus sign. In the F or U column, enter F if the variance is favorable or U if the variance is unfavorable.
tasks.explanation:
Actual direct labor rate: $394,240 / 17,600 hours = $22.40 per hour.
Standard hours allowed: 12,000 units x 1.50 hours = 18,000 hours.

Direct labor rate variance: ($22.40 - $22.00) x 17,600 actual hours = $7,040 unfavorable. The senior operators scheduled in March earn more than the standard rate.

Direct labor efficiency variance: (17,600 actual hours - 18,000 standard hours) x $22.00 standard rate = $8,800 favorable. The plant used 400 fewer hours than the standard allows for 12,000 units.

Variable overhead spending variance: actual variable overhead of $163,680 - (17,600 actual hours x $9.00 standard rate = $158,400) = $5,280 unfavorable.

Variable overhead efficiency variance: (17,600 actual hours - 18,000 standard hours) x $9.00 = $3,600 favorable. Because variable overhead is applied on direct labor hours, the hours saved produce a favorable overhead efficiency variance as well.
references: Cost accounting — standard costing: direct labor rate and efficiency variances
Cost accounting — standard costing: variable overhead spending and efficiency variances

tasks.title: Total Sales Price Variance
tasks.instruction: Compute the total sales price variance for March Year 6 for the two product lines combined, using actual units sold and the difference between the actual average selling price and the budgeted selling price (in whole dollars, no commas). Enter an unfavorable variance as a positive number and a favorable variance as a negative number.
tasks.explanation:
The sales price variance is (actual selling price - budgeted selling price) x actual units sold, computed for each product line.

Ridgeline: ($92.50 - $95.00) x 14,300 units = $35,750 unfavorable, because the promotional discount pushed the average price $2.50 below budget.
Summit: ($143.00 - $140.00) x 7,700 units = $23,100 favorable.

Total: $35,750 unfavorable - $23,100 favorable = $12,650 unfavorable, entered as a positive $12,650.
tasks.explanationJa:
販売価格差異 =（実際販売単価 − 予算販売単価）× **実際**販売数量（製品ごとに計算して合算）

1. Ridgeline:（$92.50 − $95.00）× 14,300個 = −$35,750 → 値引きにより **$35,750 の不利差異**
2. Summit:（$143.00 − $140.00）× 7,700個 = +$23,100 → **$23,100 の有利差異**
3. 合計: $35,750 U − $23,100 F = **$12,650 の不利差異** → 正の数 12650 を入力

価格差異では数量は**実際販売数量**で固定する。数量の増減の影響は数量差異・ミックス差異の側で測るため、ここで予算数量を使うと効果が混ざる。
references: Cost accounting — sales price variance analysis

tasks.title: Sales Mix and Sales Quantity Variance Schedule
tasks.instruction: Complete the schedule of sales mix and sales quantity variances for March Year 6. Compute both variances using the budgeted contribution margin per unit and the budgeted sales mix. Enter whole dollars with no commas, entering an unfavorable variance as a positive number and a favorable variance as a negative number.
tasks.explanation:
Budgeted sales mix: Ridgeline 12,000 / 20,000 = 60%; Summit 8,000 / 20,000 = 40%. Actual total units sold: 22,000.

Units at actual total volume and budgeted mix: Ridgeline 22,000 x 60% = 13,200; Summit 22,000 x 40% = 8,800.

Sales mix variance = (actual units - units at budgeted mix) x budgeted contribution margin per unit.
Ridgeline: (14,300 - 13,200) x $30 = $33,000 favorable, entered as -33,000.
Summit: (7,700 - 8,800) x $50 = $55,000 unfavorable, entered as 55,000.
Total: $22,000 unfavorable, entered as 22,000.

Sales quantity variance = (actual total units - budgeted total units) x budgeted mix percentage x budgeted contribution margin per unit.
Ridgeline: (22,000 - 20,000) x 60% x $30 = $36,000 favorable, entered as -36,000.
Summit: (22,000 - 20,000) x 40% x $50 = $40,000 favorable, entered as -40,000.
Total: $76,000 favorable, entered as -76,000.

Proof: the two components sum to the total sales volume variance of $54,000 favorable ($22,000 unfavorable mix + $76,000 favorable quantity). The same total is obtained directly as (14,300 - 12,000) x $30 = $69,000 favorable for Ridgeline plus (7,700 - 8,000) x $50 = $15,000 unfavorable for Summit.
tasks.explanationJa:
販売数量差異（volume variance）は、**ミックス差異**と**数量差異**に分解できる。どちらも**予算貢献利益（CM）単価**で評価する。

**準備**
- 予算ミックス: Ridgeline 12,000/20,000 = 60%、Summit 8,000/20,000 = 40%
- 実際販売合計: 22,000個
- 「実際合計数量 × 予算ミックス」: Ridgeline 13,200個、Summit 8,800個

**1. ミックス差異 =（実際数量 − 実際合計×予算ミックス）× 予算CM単価**
- Ridgeline:（14,300 − 13,200）× $30 = +$33,000 → 有利なので **−33000**
- Summit:（7,700 − 8,800）× $50 = −$55,000 → 不利なので **55000**
- 合計: **22000**（$22,000 の不利差異）

CM単価の低いRidgeline（$30）へ構成比が傾き、高いSummit（$50）の比率が下がったため、合計では不利になる。

**2. 数量差異 =（実際合計数量 − 予算合計数量）× 予算ミックス × 予算CM単価**
- Ridgeline:（22,000 − 20,000）× 60% × $30 = +$36,000 → **−36000**
- Summit:（22,000 − 20,000）× 40% × $50 = +$40,000 → **−40000**
- 合計: **−76000**（$76,000 の有利差異）

**3. 検算**
$22,000 U + $76,000 F = $54,000 の有利差異。
製品別に直接計算しても、（14,300 − 12,000）× $30 = $69,000 F と（7,700 − 8,000）× $50 = −$15,000 U の合計で $54,000 F となり一致する。

総販売数量は予算を10%上回った一方で、構成比は低採算品に傾いた、というのが3月の売上の姿である。
references: Cost accounting — sales mix variance analysis
Cost accounting — sales quantity variance analysis

tasks.title: Interpretation of the March Variances
tasks.instruction: Select each statement that is supported by the variances computed in the preceding work tabs and by the information in the exhibits. Select all that apply.
options: The favorable direct labor efficiency variance is consistent with staffing the March schedule with senior operators, who completed the output in fewer hours than the standard allows.
The unfavorable direct materials quantity variance is consistent with the off-specification steel bought on the spot market, which generated scrap above the standard allowance.
The unfavorable sales mix variance reflects a shift in the sales mix toward Ridgeline, which carries the lower budgeted contribution margin per unit.
The unfavorable variable overhead spending variance arose because the plant worked fewer direct labor hours than the standard hours allowed for the output produced.
The favorable sales quantity variance shows that both product lines were sold at average selling prices above their budgeted selling prices.
The total direct materials variance is favorable, because the premium paid per pound was more than offset by the pounds saved in production.
correctAnswer: The favorable direct labor efficiency variance is consistent with staffing the March schedule with senior operators, who completed the output in fewer hours than the standard allows.
The unfavorable direct materials quantity variance is consistent with the off-specification steel bought on the spot market, which generated scrap above the standard allowance.
The unfavorable sales mix variance reflects a shift in the sales mix toward Ridgeline, which carries the lower budgeted contribution margin per unit.
tasks.explanation:
Supported statements:

- The direct labor efficiency variance is $8,800 favorable because 17,600 hours were worked against 18,000 standard hours allowed. Scheduling senior operators is consistent with completing the output in fewer hours, and the same crew decision explains the $7,040 unfavorable rate variance.
- The direct materials quantity variance is $15,600 unfavorable, reflecting 2,400 pounds used above the standard allowance, which is consistent with the scrap reported on the off-specification spot-market lots.
- The sales mix variance is $22,000 unfavorable because Ridgeline rose to 65% of actual units (14,300 of 22,000) against a budgeted 60%, and Ridgeline carries a $30 budgeted contribution margin against $50 for Summit.

Statements that are not supported:

- The variable overhead spending variance of $5,280 unfavorable compares the $163,680 incurred with the $158,400 that should have been incurred for the 17,600 hours actually worked. Working fewer hours than standard produces the $3,600 favorable variable overhead efficiency variance instead.
- The sales quantity variance isolates the effect of total volume (22,000 actual units against 20,000 budgeted) while holding the budgeted mix and budgeted contribution margin constant, so it carries no information about selling prices. Ridgeline in fact sold at $92.50 against a budgeted $95.00.
- The total direct materials variance is $10,080 + $15,600 = $25,680 unfavorable, because both the price paid per pound and the pounds consumed exceeded standard.
tasks.explanationJa:
**支持される記述**

1. 直接労務の能率差異は $8,800 の有利差異（17,600時間 対 標準許容18,000時間）。熟練工を多く配置したという記述と整合し、同じ人員配置が賃率差異 $7,040 の不利差異も説明する。
2. 直接材料の数量差異は $15,600 の不利差異（標準より2,400ポンド超過）。規格外のスポット材で仕損が増えたという記述と整合する。
3. ミックス差異は $22,000 の不利差異。実際構成比はRidgelineが65%（14,300/22,000）で予算の60%を上回り、CM単価の低い製品（$30 対 Summit $50）へ寄ったためである。

**支持されない記述**

- 変動製造間接費の予算差異 $5,280 U は、実際発生額 $163,680 と「実際作業時間17,600時間に対して発生すべき額 $158,400」の比較である。時間が標準より少なかったことの効果は能率差異 $3,600 F の側に出る。両者を取り違えないこと。
- 数量差異は予算ミックスと予算CMを固定したまま**総販売数量**（22,000個 対 予算20,000個）の効果だけを切り出すもので、販売単価の情報は含まない。実際、Ridgelineは $92.50 と予算 $95.00 を下回って販売している。
- 直接材料の総差異は $10,080 + $15,600 = $25,680 の**不利**差異。単価も消費量も標準を超過しており、有利差異は生じていない。
references: Cost accounting — interpretation of standard cost variances
Cost accounting — sales price, volume, and mix analysis

subject: BAR
title: Cast-Iron Cookware: Manufacturing Cost and Sales Variances
scenario: Ironwood Cookware, Inc. manufactures cast-iron skillets and uses a standard costing system. Direct materials price variances are isolated at the time of purchase, and raw materials inventory is carried at standard cost. Variable and fixed manufacturing overhead are applied on the basis of standard direct labor hours (DLH) allowed for actual output. The controller has asked you to prepare the March 20X5 variance report for the 10-inch skillet line, analyze the sales results for the two skillet sizes, and interpret the results using the operations memo. Use the standard cost card in **Exhibit 1**, the March actual production data in **Exhibit 2**, the sales data in **Exhibit 3**, and the operations memo in **Exhibit 4**.

exhibits.title: Exhibit 1: Standard Cost Card — 10-Inch Skillet (per unit)
exhibits.content:
| Cost element | Standard quantity | Standard price | Standard cost per skillet |
|---|---|---|---|
| Direct materials (pig iron) | 4.0 lb | $1.50 per lb | $6.00 |
| Direct labor | 0.5 DLH | $24.00 per DLH | $12.00 |
| Variable manufacturing overhead | 0.5 DLH | $10.00 per DLH | $5.00 |
| Fixed manufacturing overhead | 0.5 DLH | $18.00 per DLH | $9.00 |
| **Total standard manufacturing cost** | | | **$32.00** |

The fixed overhead rate is based on budgeted monthly fixed overhead of $360,000 and a denominator level of 20,000 DLH (40,000 skillets).

exhibits.title: Exhibit 2: March 20X5 Actual Production Data — 10-Inch Skillet
exhibits.content:
| Item | Actual |
|---|---|
| Skillets produced (all good units) | 38,000 |
| Pig iron purchased | 170,000 lb for $241,400 |
| Pig iron used in production | 158,000 lb |
| Pig iron on hand, March 1 | 22,000 lb |
| Direct labor | 19,800 hours costing $485,100 |
| Variable manufacturing overhead incurred | $205,900 |
| Fixed manufacturing overhead incurred | $368,500 |
| Variable selling cost per skillet sold | $3.00 |
| Fixed selling and administrative costs | $210,000 |

exhibits.title: Exhibit 3: March 20X5 Sales Data
exhibits.content:
| Product | Budgeted units | Budgeted price | Budgeted contribution margin per unit | Actual units sold | Actual price |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10-inch skillet | 30,000 | $42.00 | $16.00 | 31,200 | $41.00 |
| 12-inch skillet | 20,000 | $55.00 | $22.00 | 16,800 | $57.00 |

Sales variances are measured on a contribution margin basis using budgeted contribution margins per unit.

exhibits.title: Exhibit 4: Operations Memo — March 20X5
exhibits.content:
To: Controller
From: Plant Manager

1. Effective March 1, purchasing switched to a new supplier offering a lower grade of pig iron at a discount. The casting line reported more defective castings that had to be scrapped and re-poured, and finishing crews spent additional time grinding rough surfaces.
2. A new wage agreement took effect on March 1, raising the average hourly rate paid to casting and finishing crews.
3. The main furnace was shut down for two days in mid-March for an unscheduled refractory repair, reducing the number of skillets produced below the monthly plan.
4. The regional utility increased its electricity tariff during March.

tasks.title: Direct Materials and Direct Labor Variances
tasks.instruction: Compute each variance for March 20X5. Enter the amount in whole dollars, no commas, as a positive number. In the F or U column, enter F for favorable or U for unfavorable.
tasks.explanation: Materials price variance (isolated at purchase) = (actual price - standard price) x quantity PURCHASED. Actual price = $241,400 / 170,000 lb = $1.42; ($1.42 - $1.50) x 170,000 = $13,600 F. Using the 158,000 lb used would give $12,640, which is incorrect when the variance is isolated at purchase. Materials quantity variance = (actual quantity USED - standard quantity allowed) x standard price = (158,000 - 38,000 x 4.0 = 152,000) x $1.50 = $9,000 U. Labor rate variance = (actual rate - standard rate) x actual hours; actual rate = $485,100 / 19,800 = $24.50; ($24.50 - $24.00) x 19,800 = $9,900 U. Labor efficiency variance = (actual hours - standard hours allowed) x standard rate = (19,800 - 38,000 x 0.5 = 19,000) x $24 = $19,200 U.
references: Standard costing — direct cost variance analysis

tasks.title: Journal Entry for the Pig Iron Purchase
tasks.instruction: Prepare the journal entry to record the March purchase of pig iron on account. Enter amounts in whole dollars, no commas. Enter 0 in cells that should have no amount.
tasks.explanation: Because raw materials inventory is carried at standard cost and the price variance is isolated at purchase, raw materials inventory is debited at standard: 170,000 lb x $1.50 = $255,000. Accounts payable is credited for the actual cost of $241,400. The $13,600 difference is a favorable price variance and is recorded as a credit. Debits $255,000 = credits $241,400 + $13,600.
references: Standard costing — journal entries for variances

tasks.title: Manufacturing Overhead Variances
tasks.instruction: Using a four-variance analysis, compute each overhead variance for March 20X5. Enter the amount in whole dollars, no commas, as a positive number. In the F or U column, enter F for favorable or U for unfavorable.
tasks.explanation: Variable overhead spending = actual VOH - (actual hours x standard rate) = $205,900 - 19,800 x $10 ($198,000) = $7,900 U. Variable overhead efficiency = (actual hours - standard hours allowed) x standard rate = (19,800 - 19,000) x $10 = $8,000 U. Fixed overhead budget variance = actual FOH - budgeted FOH = $368,500 - $360,000 = $8,500 U. Fixed overhead production-volume variance = budgeted FOH - applied FOH = $360,000 - (19,000 standard hours x $18 = $342,000) = $18,000 U. Applied fixed overhead is based on standard hours allowed for actual output, not on actual hours.

tasks.title: Total Underapplied Overhead
tasks.instruction: Compute the total manufacturing overhead (variable plus fixed) underapplied or overapplied for March 20X5. Enter the amount in whole dollars, no commas, as a positive number if underapplied and as a negative number if overapplied.
tasks.explanation: Actual overhead = $205,900 + $368,500 = $574,400. Applied overhead = 19,000 standard hours x ($10 + $18) = $532,000. Underapplied overhead = $574,400 - $532,000 = $42,400, which equals the sum of the four overhead variances ($7,900 + $8,000 + $8,500 + $18,000).

tasks.title: Interpreting the Variance Pattern
tasks.instruction: The controller notes that the direct materials price variance is favorable while the direct materials quantity variance and the direct labor efficiency variance are both unfavorable. Select the event in Exhibit 4 that most likely explains this combination of variances.
options: The switch to the lower-grade pig iron supplier
The new wage agreement effective March 1
The increase in the electricity tariff
tasks.correctAnswer: The switch to the lower-grade pig iron supplier
tasks.explanation: Buying lower-grade pig iron at a discount produces a favorable price variance. Lower-grade material causes more defective castings (more pounds used per good skillet, an unfavorable quantity variance) and more re-pouring and grinding time (more hours per good skillet, an unfavorable labor efficiency variance and, because overhead is applied on DLH, an unfavorable variable overhead efficiency variance). The wage agreement explains only the unfavorable labor rate variance. The furnace shutdown reduced output and explains the unfavorable fixed overhead production-volume variance, not a favorable materials price variance. The electricity tariff increase explains the unfavorable variable overhead spending variance. Purchasing should not be evaluated solely on its favorable price variance when it causes larger unfavorable variances downstream.
tasks.explanationJa:
**低品質材料を値引きで購入** → 価格差異は**有利**
→ 不良鋳物が増え材料を多く使う → 数量差異**不利**
→ 再鋳造・研磨に時間がかかる → 労務能率差異**不利**（DLH基準の変動間接費能率差異も不利）

この3つを同時に説明できるのは材料サプライヤー変更のみ。

他の事象との対応:
- 新賃金協定 → 労務**賃率**差異の不利のみ
- 炉の停止 → 生産量減 → 固定費**操業度**差異の不利（材料価格の有利は説明できない）
- 電気料金の値上げ → 変動間接費**予算差異**の不利

実務上の含意: 購買部門を価格差異の有利だけで評価すると、製造部門の不利差異（合計 9,000 + 19,200 + 8,000 = 36,200）が価格差異の有利 13,600 を上回る点を見落とす。
references: Standard costing — variance investigation and responsibility

tasks.title: Sales Price, Mix, and Quantity Variances
tasks.instruction: Using Exhibit 3, compute the total sales price variance, the sales mix variance, and the sales quantity variance for both skillet sizes combined, on a contribution margin basis. Enter the amount in whole dollars, no commas, as a positive number. In the F or U column, enter F for favorable or U for unfavorable.
tasks.explanation: Sales price variance = (actual price - budgeted price) x actual units: 10-inch ($41 - $42) x 31,200 = $31,200 U; 12-inch ($57 - $55) x 16,800 = $33,600 F; net $2,400 F. Budgeted mix = 30,000 / 50,000 = 60% 10-inch and 40% 12-inch. Actual total units = 48,000. Sales mix variance = (actual units - actual total units x budgeted mix %) x budgeted CM: 10-inch (31,200 - 28,800) x $16 = $38,400 F; 12-inch (16,800 - 19,200) x $22 = $52,800 U; net $14,400 U. The mix shifted toward the lower-margin 10-inch skillet. Sales quantity variance = (actual total units - budgeted total units) x budgeted weighted-average CM per unit = (48,000 - 50,000) x $18.40 (0.60 x $16 + 0.40 x $22) = $36,800 U. Check: mix $14,400 U + quantity $36,800 U = sales volume variance of $51,200 U = 10-inch (1,200 x $16 = $19,200 F) + 12-inch (-3,200 x $22 = $70,400 U).
tasks.explanationJa:
**売上価格差異** = (実際価格 − 予算価格) × 実際数量
- 10インチ: (41 − 42) × 31,200 = 31,200 U
- 12インチ: (57 − 55) × 16,800 = 33,600 F
- 合計 **2,400 F**

**ミックス差異** = (実際数量 − 実際総数量 × 予算構成比) × 予算CM
- 予算構成比: 10インチ 60%（30,000/50,000）、12インチ 40%
- 実際総数量 48,000
- 10インチ: (31,200 − 28,800) × 16 = 38,400 F
- 12インチ: (16,800 − 19,200) × 22 = 52,800 U
- 合計 **14,400 U**（低CMの10インチに構成がシフト）

**数量差異** = (実際総数量 − 予算総数量) × 予算加重平均CM
- 加重平均CM = 0.6 × 16 + 0.4 × 22 = 18.40
- (48,000 − 50,000) × 18.40 = **36,800 U**

検証: ミックス14,400 U + 数量36,800 U = 販売数量差異51,200 U（製品別: 19,200 F − 70,400 U）。

誤答パターン: 10インチの数量が予算を上回っているので「有利」と考えがちだが、ミックス差異は**実際総数量に予算構成比を掛けた量**と比べる。
references: Sales variance analysis — price, mix, and quantity

tasks.title: Meaning of the Production-Volume Variance
tasks.instruction: Select the statement that best describes the cause and meaning of the March fixed overhead production-volume variance.
options: Fixed overhead costs incurred exceeded the monthly fixed overhead budget
Actual direct labor hours exceeded the standard hours allowed for the skillets produced
Good output required fewer standard direct labor hours than the 20,000-hour denominator level, so less fixed overhead was applied than budgeted
The wage agreement increased the fixed overhead rate per direct labor hour
tasks.correctAnswer: Good output required fewer standard direct labor hours than the 20,000-hour denominator level, so less fixed overhead was applied than budgeted
tasks.explanation: The production-volume variance compares budgeted fixed overhead ($360,000) with fixed overhead applied to good output (19,000 standard hours x $18 = $342,000). Producing 38,000 skillets instead of the 40,000-unit denominator level (the furnace shutdown) left $18,000 of fixed capacity cost unabsorbed. It does not represent a spending overrun; spending above budget is the $8,500 fixed overhead budget variance. Actual hours exceeding standard hours is the efficiency variance, and the wage agreement affects the labor rate variance, not the fixed overhead rate.
tasks.explanationJa:
操業度差異 = 予算固定費 360,000 − 配賦額（標準時間19,000 × 18 = 342,000）= 18,000 U。

実際の良品生産38,000個が基準操業度40,000個（20,000 DLH）を下回ったため（炉の停止）、固定費が配賦しきれなかったことを示す。**支出の超過ではない**。

他の記述の誤り:
- 固定費の実際額が予算を超過 → それは**予算差異**（8,500 U）
- 実際時間が標準時間を超過 → それは**能率差異**
- 賃金協定 → 労務**賃率**差異に影響し、固定費配賦率は変わらない
